items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: You know what? I've been thinkin' 'bout all this, tryin' to make sense of it all.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Grown-ups are always comin' up with fairy tales to make us kids toe the line. Not me, though.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Witches by the pond, demons under the bed ... Once you've had a thought through all the "whys," it ain't hard to see they're just grown-up fibs.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: But this time, things are a tad trickier than usual.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: A world full of wonders, a best mate I could only dream of, a bunch of cheeky fairies, a terrifyin' monster, some magical trinkets. Overall, one heart-poundin' adventure ...

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: All those fairy tale things appeared out of nowhere, right before me eyes, like an adventure book made special for me.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: If this were a riddle, what'd the answer be? That's what I was thinking about.

items.speaker: Lamplighter
items.text: So, do you know?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Yes. You gave me a clue, didn't ya?

items.speaker: Lamplighter
items.text: Of course, we are! Critters have called this place home since before anyone can remember.

items.speaker: Lamplighter
items.text: Only thing is, it looks different to each person who enters it. Most folks can't manage to find their way into "this" Cross Street.

items.speaker: Lamplighter
items.text: And it's even harder if there's no one to guide you.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Right from the start, I had a feeling the critters were a bit familiar.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: That tomb watcher fella, the lady and her flowers, them cheeky critters at the club, and that Packleader Girt ...

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: That tomb watcher might seem big and tough, but he's softer than he looks. To him, being well-thought of by the others is what mattered most.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: He's just like my dad.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: What I said to the tomb watcher, it's really what I've been wanting to say to me dad. I've always wished he wouldn't care so much about what other people think.
Lamplighter is silent, watching Flutterpage as though encouraging her to continue.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: The lady in the garden, she's a bit like me mum. Though, let's be clear, my mum ain't near half as frightenin'!

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: But she fusses over her weavin' just the same as that lady in the garden did her flowers.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Mum's always knitting and weaving every day just to make ends meet, and all the while I ain't seen her smile over one thing she made, not even those cute little scarves.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: I always keep me distance, worried that she might bite my head off or somethin', but I know she's working herself to the bone for us and I just wish she could find a bit happiness in her work again. I guess what I oughta tell her is that those scarves of hers are beautiful.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: As for Girt, I know exactly who she is—my sister, Sarah.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: She's so bloomin' proud of herself, and everything's gotta go her way. And like Girt did with those pups, she always treats me like I'm just a kid. Sometimes that really ticks me off.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: If there's a chance, I s'pose I'll try to surprise Sarah and make her proud of me, just like how them puppies did with their boss.
Flutterpage gives a cheeky grin and makes a silly face at Lamplighter.
She achieves the desired effect, and Lamplighter laughs gently.

items.speaker: Lamplighter
items.text: How about the others?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: The rest? Well, them critters at the club are a bit like my schoolmates.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Every day's the same with them, jabberin' about the same old rubbish. They all look and sound alike to me like they was just repeating each other. Drive me barmy, they do.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: But maybe I was wrong about 'em—like I was those critters. For all their chattering, that little stone really was their "dearest possession." Otherwise, the fireflies wouldn't have hidden there.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: And that library lady, the one who reckons she knows it all.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Maybe she does got all the answers, but I ain't gonna go askin' her every little thing. And who's to say she ain't just feeding me a load 'o cobblers? I'd have no way of tellin'.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: I gotta figure these sorts of answers for myself. So ...

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: I s'pose the Administrator's a bit like me, ain't she? I shouldn't be relying on people for everything. It's my job to find me own answers.

items.speaker: Lamplighter
items.text: Now that's a very interesting thought. So then who's left?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: The Bananach. Though I still ain't sure what it was, to be honest. But I've got a strange feeling about it.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: What a creepy thing—going after kids without names. It whispered all sorts of rubbish to me, like "give up," tryin' to make me "stay here forever" ...

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: I guess that's got something to do with you, don't it?
Eyes slightly wide open, Lamplighter seems to have heard an unexpected answer. Flutterpage is also confused by her reaction.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Oh? You telling me that ain't so?

items.speaker: Lamplighter
items.text: I'm just curious. Why you'd think it'd have anything to do with me?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: I suppose ... because you said this thing was horrible, but it turned out ... Hmm, I guess I'm wrong. It isn't you, not exactly.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Maybe it's those fears in your mind that you only think are scary. Uh, I'm not sure how to put it, but it's all those scary and annoying things we gotta face sometimes.
Flutterpage waves her arms in the air, hoping to find the right word for the strange entity, but nothing ever quite fits.

items.speaker: Lamplighter
items.text: Then you're saying I'm the one behind all this? I'm the big baddie?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: I didn't say nothin' like that.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Because everything, everything here ...
Flutterpage flings her arms open, like she's drawing a line from one edge of the world to the other.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: None of it's real.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: C'mon, of course it's all made-up nonsense. Fun nonsense, but still. I'm eleven years old, ya know!

items.speaker: Lamplighter
items.text: So, then what is all this?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: That's the question I've been turnin' over in me head all this time.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: I'm thinking, when did all this start?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: It weren't on that strange Cross Street, and it weren't in the woods where the Bananach started chasin' us. It was right here.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: I suppose, maybe it's 'cause I opened this bag here. That's when all this started.

items.speaker: Lamplighter
items.text: You're saying it all started with that little pouch?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: That's what I reckoned at first, until I remembered that story about the lake.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Sure are! 'Bout witches dragging people into the water, and fairies thieving stuff ... There are loads of them.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: But I remembered somethin'. Dad told me one of the saddest stories of 'em all.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: The tale says, years ago, there was a little girl—just about my age, and ... well, she went through a lot of horrible things.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: She was sad and disappointed, so off she goes to the lake, leavin' all the things what made her miserable behind for good.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: That's why the grown-ups don't want other kids coming 'round here.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: 'Cause that little girl was you, wasn't it?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: So, it didn't begin with the bag. It was me laying here, makin' that wish.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: I was down in the dumps back then, and made a wish to fly off to someplace different.

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: I want to be like you, then I could fly, fly off somewhere else.

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: Might be somewhere else. There's an exciting adventure waitin' for me, far away from all these worries.

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: Could you take me there?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: You're here all because I made a wish.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: It was you that swiped my name, all so I'd forget the past and stay here with you, in this "somewhere else."

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Lamplighter. The last letter of my name ... you've got it in your hand, ain't you?

items.speaker: Lamplighter
items.text: That I do.
Lamplighter unclenches her hand, and the last lost flitter of light escapes.

items.speaker: Lamplighter
items.text: This is the last letter of your name. Take it, and you won't forget anything about yourself. You can go back to where you came from.

items.speaker: Lamplighter
items.text: But, is that what you really want?

items.speaker: Lamplighter
items.text: Your world isn't like this one. It doesn't hold the same kind of beauty. You've seen that by now, haven't you?

items.speaker: Lamplighter
items.text: There's a limit to what your winds can clear. You won't find an answer to every question.

items.speaker: Lamplighter
items.text: Flutterpage, my friend, I really like you. Stay with me, won't you?

items.speaker: Lamplighter
items.text: You'd never have a dull moment, I swear it. We'd be happy every day. Doesn't that sound wonderful?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: No.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Sorry. Thanks for the invite, and for answerin' me wish, but, I s'pose I don't truly wanna leave my home behind.

items.speaker: Lamplighter
items.text: Because of your family?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Yes, they may drive me up the wall, but I still love 'em, don't I?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: But it's not just 'cause of them.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: When we met, remember me saying I couldn't wrap my head 'round Sarah's "There's no why"? I said, grown-ups musta known sometimes there weren't no why.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: But that's a load of rubbish. Truth is, I know the answer, only I've been hiding from it.

items.speaker: Lamplighter
items.text: So, what do you think the answer is?

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: That is: there's no why without a reason why.

items.speaker: Lamplighter
items.text: Heh ...

items.speaker: Lamplighter
items.text: Hahaha! Your answer is even more of a tongue twister than the question!
Lamplighter smiles, not in the same dark way as before; it makes Flutterpage want to smile along with her.
And so Flutterpage chuckles along.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Hehe, I know, I was thinkin' the same thing.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: But that's my answer, and I'm stickin' to it. I'm sure of that.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: I ain't saying Sarah and the others are lying. "There's no why" might well be her answer, but that don't mean it's gotta be mine.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Nothing will stop me finding the answer myself. I'll keep thinking and asking questions, even if no one can answer me.

items.speaker: Lamplighter
items.text: That is a wonderful answer.

items.speaker: Lamplighter
items.text: You've really surprised me, Flutterpage.
With a soft chuckle, Lamplighter finally lets the firefly stumble its way over to Flutterpage.
It settles on Flutterpage's shoulder and blends into the moonlight, lighting up the lingering darkness in the girl's heart.

items.speaker: Lamplighter
items.text: My friend, Liberti Grove, you did it.

items.speaker: Lamplighter
items.text: You've chosen a difficult path, one I couldn't choose for myself.

items.speaker: Lamplighter
items.text: And I ... I'll respect your decision, and I wish you all the best from the bottom of my heart.

items.speaker: Lamplighter
items.text: It's alright. This is just a parting of ways. I've grown used to it.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Lamplighter, I ...

items.speaker: Lamplighter
items.text: Don't make that sad face, Liberti.

items.speaker: Lamplighter
items.text: After this, you'll forget all about me and what happened here, and then you'll meet new friends and go on new adventures.

items.speaker: Lamplighter
items.text: But that's only fair. You're a sweet girl, and you deserve to have many more friends.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Hang on! New friends or not, you're still my best mate! I'll never forget you.
Flutterpage's frantic words fall on deaf ears as Lamplighter offers nothing but a smile. A silent, broken smile.

items.speaker: Lamplighter
items.text: It's time.
She raises her stick again and strikes the ground.
Though she does so gently this time, the sound of the staff striking the ground rings deafeningly in Flutterpage's ears.
The lamp in Lamplighter's hand erupts with light, casting a brilliance far surpassing anything before it.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: This is ... the sun, it's risin'!

items.speaker: Lamplighter
items.text: Yes. It's time to awaken from your dream.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: No! I still have more I want—

items.speaker: Lamplighter
items.text: Goodbye, my friend.
Liberti.

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: zzzZZZ
Liberti!

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: Not now ... Ollie ...
Oh ...

items.speaker: Sarah
items.text: This ain't a chicken coop, and I'm not your bleedin' rooster! Now get up, you little so-and-so!

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: Whoa?!

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: Sis? I'm ...

items.speaker: Sarah
items.text: Sent you out for a bit of shopping, and instead you stay out all night?! All 'cause you got a scolding, you decide to turn into a little runaway riff-raff?

items.speaker: Sarah
items.text: Have you any idea how long we've all been searching for you? You're in for it now!

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: What? I didn't ... Wait. I've been gone a whole night?
Indeed, the morning light shines warmly, but for Liberti, the events of the previous night have faded into a blank haze.

items.speaker: Sarah
items.text: Was it the sweets? All this on account of me saying I wouldn't let you get any?
With a sharp frown, Sarah fishes out a handful of candies and slaps them into Liberti's palm.

items.speaker: Sarah
items.text: There you go! And here I thought I was teaching you about the value of money. We're not made of the stuff, but we're not penniless either! If you're so desperate for a bit of candy, speak up instead of pulling stunts like this.

items.speaker: Sarah
items.text: What? Not enough for you? Let me tell you right now, don't you dream of expecting an apology from me.

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: I didn't have me hopes up or nothin'. Still, thanks, sis.
Liberti puts the candy in her pocket and discovers something else hidden within.

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: Did—Did I fold this?
Liberti looks at the bird, and a faint memory surfaces. She set this bird free, letting it fly into the sky.
And at that moment, in her memory, someone else was there with her.
A sensation lingers in Liberti's heart, leaving her feeling as though she has lost something. She unfolds the paper bird in her hands.

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: Potatoes, bread, three cans o' beans, cabbage, carrots, and ...

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: And ...
Her eyes lock in place.
At the very bottom of the shopping list, a line of elegant handwriting stands out from the scrawl above it.

items.speaker: Sarah
items.text: "Flutterpage" ... What's a "Flutterpage"?

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: It's ... It's ...

items.speaker: Bird
items.text: Chirps.

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: It's you!
The familiar bird from before returns.
It lands on Liberti's shoulder, tilting its head as its shining eyes meet hers.
Like a spark cutting through the fog, a vivid memory leaps to life in Liberti's mind.

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: This is a name.

items.speaker: Liberti
items.text: My other name.
Though her recollections are still hazy, an inexplicable feeling reveals the answer to her.
It is a gift, sent to her from her mysterious friend, wrapped in the most beautiful of blessings.

items.speaker: Bird
items.text: Chirps.
The little bird flutters its wings and alights from her shoulder.
It glides up over the eaves and soars above the streets of London, riding the wind into the distant horizon.
